voiceover: You run git reset hard, and an hour of commits vanishes. Your stomach drops. Breathe: they're probably not gone. Git keeps a log of where HEAD and your branches have pointed, called the reflog. Run git reflog and you'll see your recent positions, each with a commit hash. Find the one from before you messed up, and create a branch there to get it back. Commits nothing points to only get cleaned up later by garbage collection, by default after weeks. Two catches: the reflog only lives on your machine, and changes you never committed aren't in it at all. So commit often. Send this to a friend before their next panic.
